how_to_read.speaker: the player character whose secret backstory this is: the upload's speaker
how_to_read.knowers: who knows the row before anything public names it. With no knowers field: the speaker, and every person or creature on the row (a pair's two ends, an event's who), since what happens between two is known to both (#4523 ruling C). Otherwise a list of names (the only knowers), "party" (all four player characters), "everyone" (common knowledge) or "dm" (nobody: a real secret, not even the speaker). A node with no knowers is known to the speaker and to itself if it is a person
how_to_read.tier: stated = the words are in the text; inferred = only implied (offered to the DM as a suggestion, never extracted as a fact)
how_to_read.must_find: false = a good find if present, not a miss if absent
how_to_read.current: false = history: it was true and is not now
how_to_read.line: the line of the document's plain-text export that supports it (blank lines count)
how_to_read.reveals: lore_key.json's reveals lists, by id, the rows of this key the public lore states; judged by what the lore says, row by row, never by matching ends alone
how_to_read.threads: kind quest, hook or mystery; taker = whose own pursuit it is; same_as = the lore key's thread for the same story
